rv: William "One Shot" Beaudine was one of the most prolific directors in Hollywood. He was a no-nonsense professional who was able to crank out films in as little as five days. It was said that he typically only made one take of a scene -- sometimes leaving in actors' mistakes or scenery flubs or special effects that didn't pull off correctly. rv: One of tTHE first filmed cigarette commercials on TV...

The American Tobacco Company was the first major tobacco advertiser to sponsor a "national" TV program {the short-lived "BARNEY BLAKE, POLICE REPORTER", on NBC} in 1948. They were thinking about the future of television advertising, and wanted something unique for one of their first filmed commercials. So they asked Jam Handy, who produced several "commercial" theatrical films sponsored by them over the years [best known of these was 1943's "Lucky Strike Means Fine Tobacco", featuring performances by Frank Sinatra ("YOUR HIT PARADE") and Kay Kyser's orchestra ("THE KOLLEGE OF MUSICAL KNOWLEDGE
Tobacco companies are lying to us.:cigarettes can't dance.
this is a funny advertisement for Lucky Strike Cigarretes featuring square dancing ciggarets, it's pretty cute actually.

Personally, I was appalled when the square dance caller chose to suicide by self-immolation. On the other hand, we can all see what drove him to it. So, even though this is about cigarettes, it's really a snuff film.

This is quite a novelty for me as I was born after laws were passed banning cigarette ads from U.S. TV. I think it's great that this is here as it could be of historical value to people looking at the history of cigarette marketing.

OldChine1946: A tour through the Jerry Fairbanks studios in Hollywood, showing the production of animation, TV films, industrial and advertising films.

rv: There are a few really good things here: first of all, the beautiful marvel of kitchen designe, the PreSet Table! There are some good studio shots, and a shot of nice looking fiberglass beach costume. Overall a nice piece of informative filmmaking, but the picture is much too blurred to really be 100 % enjoyable.

Quite an enjoyable romp through The Jerry Fairbanks studio, who made such amazing shorts (which can be found on here) as Freedom Highway, Century 21 Calling and Once Upon A Honeymoon. This film mainly focuses on his contributions to the Paramount industrial film collection. Something I wasnt aware of. We see tantalizing titles such as Speaking Of Animals and Potatoes Unlimited. Some overview of how these films are made when we are shown a film about fiberglass fabrics (love the fiberglass quilt). I always love Fairbanks films, so all of this was a treat. Reccomended!

dollar_store: Dollar Store is a piece of raw, silent stock footage depicting shopping scenes from a bygone era, likely intended for use in a commercial or advertising production. The film captures customers browsing through aisles filled with budget-friendly merchandise, showcasing the atmosphere of a discount retail store. Viewers note its historical value, providing a glimpse into past consumer habits, clothing choices, and store layouts. While some find it dull due to the lack of sound or narrative,…

rv: I found this film very interesting. Very useful footage. I think this film provides a rare insight into what stores used to look like. Thanks Mr Prelinger.
Hmmm, Which Dress Do I Want????

The lady with the scary hair must have pulled out six or seven of those dresses to look at, even though there were only two color schemes and they were otherwise identical. And that hair! Man, you could frighten small children into obedience by threatening them with that. "You be good or we'll take you to the hairdresser and make you look just like her!" Fun stuff!

It might not be as entertaining to watch, but this is useful stock footage of shopping and stores in the era. It probably wasn't recorded with sound. These were clearly a series of shots that they were going to cut up to turn into a commercial, not the commercial itself. The fact that footage like this is here is why this is called an archive, and not a youtube type entertainment channel.

SO while waiting for Diesel story to load, I thought I'd sneak a peak at 'Dollar Store' which essentially are outtakes from a commerical advertising the store. A woman with mile high hair, looks over a rack of dresses which all look the same. Then she looks over a teapot, a radio and a pitcher lol. Finally, there are some shots of FISHING LURES! Oooh.
